Vaccination coverage indicators

Source: vignettes/coverage-indicators.Rmd
coverage-indicators.Rmd
library(vaxsurvR)

What counts as vaccinated

A coverage figure is meaningless without the definition behind it. The same survey yields materially different numbers depending on whether a caregiver’s recollection counts as evidence.

vaxsurvR grades the evidence for each dose:

vcs_evidence_levels()
#> [1] "card_date" "card_mark" "recall"    "none"      "unknown"
vcs_evidence_definitions()
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>   definition       description                                                  
#>   <chr>            <chr>                                                        
#> 1 card             Documented on the card (with or without a date). Children wi…
#> 2 card_date        Documented on the card with a usable date. Card marks withou…
#> 3 recall           Reported by the caregiver, ignoring card documentation.      
#> 4 card_or_recall   Documented on the card OR reported by the caregiver.         
#> 5 card_then_recall Card where a card exists; caregiver recall only for children…
graded <- derive_evidence(vcs_example)
table(graded$vaccinations$evidence)
#> 
#> card_date card_mark    recall      none   unknown 
#>      1161       185       931      1270        37

Note "unknown": neither card nor recall information exists. That is different from evidence that the dose was not given, and it stays different.

Definitions give different answers 

defs <- c("card", "card_date", "recall", "card_or_recall")
results <- lapply(defs, function(e) {
  d <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example, evidence = e)
  est <- estimate_coverage(vcs_design(d), vaccines = "PENTA1")
  data.frame(evidence = e, estimate = round(est$estimate, 3),
             denominator = est$denominator)
})
do.call(rbind, results)
#>         evidence estimate denominator
#> 1           card    0.910         152
#> 2      card_date    0.893         127
#> 3         recall    0.870         247
#> 4 card_or_recall    0.907         252

card has a smaller denominator because children with no card have unknown status. That is the honest treatment: the alternative – counting them as unvaccinated – would understate coverage by the card-loss rate.

If you do want that behaviour, you have to ask for it, and it is recorded:

forced <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example, evidence = "card",
                                    missing_as_unvaccinated = TRUE)
subset(derivation_rules(forced), variable == "cov_PENTA1")$rule
#>                                                                                                                                            cov_PENTA1 
#> "vaccinated = card (Documented on the card (with or without a date). Children with no card are unknown.); missing evidence treated as not vaccinated"

The three-way table

Published coverage tables report each antigen by card, by recall, and by either source, with every enumerated child in every denominator. That is one call:

estimate_coverage_by_evidence(vcs_example, vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA3", "MCV1"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 9 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card | recall | card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 9 × 14
#>   indicator evidence       domain numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <fct>          <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       Card           <over…       138         256    0.534 0.0361    0.464
#> 2 BCG       Recall         <over…       209         256    0.804 0.0277    0.750
#> 3 BCG       Card or recall <over…       218         256    0.843 0.0242    0.795
#> 4 PENTA3    Card           <over…        82         256    0.329 0.0272    0.276
#> 5 PENTA3    Recall         <over…       130         256    0.513 0.0287    0.457
#> 6 PENTA3    Card or recall <over…       137         256    0.541 0.0304    0.482
#> 7 MCV1      Card           <over…        93         256    0.372 0.0327    0.308
#> 8 MCV1      Recall         <over…       145         256    0.578 0.0352    0.509
#> 9 MCV1      Card or recall <over…       151         256    0.601 0.0318    0.539
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>

The denominator argument makes the convention explicit. "all" (default) counts a child with no evidence from a source as not vaccinated by that source, so the card row is documented coverage among all children. "determinable" leaves such children out of that row, so the card row becomes coverage among card holders. They answer different questions; state which one a table uses.

estimate_coverage_by_evidence(vcs_example, vaccines = "PENTA3",
                              denominator = "determinable")
#> <vcs_estimate: 3 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card | recall | card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 3 × 14
#>   indicator evidence       domain numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <fct>          <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA3    Card           <over…        82         151    0.559 0.0459    0.469
#> 2 PENTA3    Recall         <over…       130         254    0.516 0.0280    0.462
#> 3 PENTA3    Card or recall <over…       137         255    0.543 0.0302    0.484
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>

When recall is asked per series

Questionnaires often ask “has the child ever received Penta?” and then “how many times?”, once per antigen rather than once per dose. vcs_recall_map() describes that structure and apply_recall_map() builds the columns the dictionary picks up through recall_dictionary_entries(); dose n is then recalled when the count is at least n. See ?apply_recall_map for a worked example.

Coverage 

d   <- derive_vaccination_status(vcs_example, evidence = "card_or_recall")
des <- vcs_design(d)

estimate_coverage(des, vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA2", "PENTA3",
                                    "MCV1"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 5 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 5 × 13
#>   indicator domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       <overall>       218         253    0.852 0.0235    0.806     0.898
#> 2 PENTA1    <overall>       227         252    0.907 0.0155    0.876     0.937
#> 3 PENTA2    <overall>       185         253    0.732 0.0276    0.678     0.787
#> 4 PENTA3    <overall>       137         255    0.543 0.0302    0.484     0.602
#> 5 MCV1      <overall>       151         253    0.608 0.0320    0.545     0.671
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>
estimate_coverage(des, vaccines = "MCV1", by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#>   evidence : card_or_recall
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#>   indicator domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 MCV1      rural  rural          70         124    0.567 0.0446    0.480
#> 2 MCV1      urban  urban          81         129    0.648 0.0450    0.559
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>

Fully vaccinated

There is no universal definition, so the dose set is an argument. The default is the last dose of every antigen series in the schedule.

schedule_final_doses(vcs_example_schedule)
#> [1] "BCG"    "OPV3"   "PENTA3" "PCV3"   "IPV1"   "MCV1"   "YF"
full <- derive_fully_vaccinated(vcs_example)
estimate_full_coverage(vcs_design(full))
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 13
#>   indicator     domain numerator denominator estimate      se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>         <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 fully_vaccin… <over…         4         254   0.0164 0.00701  0.00264    0.0301
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

A narrower, and more commonly quoted, definition:

basic <- derive_fully_vaccinated(
  vcs_example,
  vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA3", "MCV1"),
  name     = "basic_full"
)
estimate_full_coverage(vcs_design(basic), variable = "basic_full")
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 13
#>   indicator  domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>      <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 basic_full <overall>        69         253    0.276 0.0261    0.225     0.328
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

Whichever you use, the definition travels with the column:

subset(derivation_rules(basic), variable == "basic_full")$rule
#>                                                                  basic_full 
#> "basic_full = all of {BCG, PENTA3, MCV1} under evidence \"card_or_recall\""

Zero-dose children

Conventionally a child who has received no dose of a DTP-containing vaccine. The marker antigen differs between programmes, so it is an argument.

zd <- derive_zero_dose(vcs_example)
estimate_zero_dose(vcs_design(zd), by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#>   indicator domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 zero_dose rural  rural          15         123   0.118  0.0257   0.0672
#> 2 zero_dose urban  urban          10         129   0.0697 0.0196   0.0312
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>
subset(derivation_rules(zd), variable == "zero_dose")$rule
#>                                                         zero_dose 
#> "zero_dose = no dose of PENTA1 under evidence \"card_or_recall\""

Dropout

Two definitions circulate, and they do not give the same answer.

Coverage difference – the classic programme indicator, computed from two marginal coverage estimates:

estimate_dropout(des, first = "PENTA1", last = "PENTA3", method = "coverage")
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   domain   numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>        <int>       <int>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 <overal…        90         227    0.400 0.0330    0.335     0.464          252
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: deff <dbl>, indicator <chr>, method <chr>

Individual histories – the proportion of children who received the first dose but not the last, among those who received the first:

estimate_dropout(des, first = "PENTA1", last = "PENTA3", method = "individual")
#> <vcs_estimate: 1 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   indicator      domain numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>          <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA1-PENTA3… <over…        94         226    0.415 0.0291    0.358     0.472
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>, method <chr>

The individual method is the better of the two: it uses each child’s own history rather than the difference of two marginals, and its denominator is explicitly the children at risk of dropping out. The coverage method is what most programme reports quote. vaxsurvR computes both and labels which produced each row, so a report can state its choice.

estimate_dropout(des, first = "BCG", last = "MCV1", by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 2 × 15
#>   indicator        domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>            <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 BCG-MCV1 dropout rural  rural          43         100    0.433 0.0491    0.337
#> 2 BCG-MCV1 dropout urban  urban          45         115    0.371 0.0490    0.275
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>, method <chr>

Standard programme indicators are just pairs:

pairs <- list(c("PENTA1", "PENTA3"), c("BCG", "MCV1"), c("PENTA1", "MCV1"))
do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(p) {
  estimate_dropout(des, p[1], p[2])[, c("indicator", "estimate", "conf_low",
                                        "conf_high", "denominator")]
}))
#> <vcs_estimate: 3 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   indicator             estimate conf_low conf_high denominator
#>   <chr>                    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA1-PENTA3 dropout    0.415    0.358     0.472         226
#> 2 BCG-MCV1 dropout         0.400    0.332     0.468         215
#> 3 PENTA1-MCV1 dropout      0.369    0.301     0.436         224

Timeliness

Coverage says whether a dose was received. Timeliness says whether it was received in the window where it protects.

tl <- derive_timeliness(vcs_example)
table(tl$vaccinations$timeliness, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#>  early timely   late   <NA> 
#>    150    922     35   2477

Only doses with both a date of birth and a usable card date can be classified; recall carries no date, so recall-only doses are NA rather than being counted as untimely.

estimate_timely_coverage(vcs_design(tl),
                         vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1"))
#> <vcs_estimate: 4 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 4 × 13
#>   indicator domain    numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 BCG       <overall>        89          90    0.986 0.0136    0.959     1    
#> 2 PENTA1    <overall>        79         112    0.704 0.0513    0.604     0.805
#> 3 PENTA3    <overall>        64          67    0.955 0.0253    0.906     1    
#> 4 MCV1      <overall>        61          76    0.798 0.0437    0.712     0.883
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>, neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>,
#> #   ci_method <chr>

Card availability

Card-documented coverage rests on cards being seen, so the availability rate belongs in the same table as the coverage it conditions.

estimate_card_availability(vcs_design(vcs_example), by = ~stratum)
#> <vcs_estimate: 2 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 2 × 14
#>   indicator domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 card_seen rural  rural          70         126    0.539 0.0442    0.453
#> 2 card_seen urban  urban          79         130    0.619 0.0394    0.541
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>

Assembling a report 

rep <- vcs_coverage_report(des,
                           vaccines = c("BCG", "PENTA1", "PENTA3", "MCV1"),
                           by = ~stratum)
rep
#> <vcs_report: 3 table(s)>
#>   coverage           4 x 13
#>   coverage_by_domain 8 x 14
#>   dropout            4 x 15
rep$dropout
#> <vcs_estimate: 4 row(s)>
#> # A tibble: 4 × 15
#>   indicator        domain stratum numerator denominator estimate     se conf_low
#>   <chr>            <chr>  <chr>       <dbl>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 PENTA1-PENTA3 d… rural  rural          57         107    0.530 0.0341    0.463
#> 2 PENTA1-PENTA3 d… urban  urban          37         119    0.310 0.0412    0.229
#> 3 BCG-MCV1 dropout rural  rural          43         100    0.433 0.0491    0.337
#> 4 BCG-MCV1 dropout urban  urban          45         115    0.371 0.0490    0.275
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: conf_high <dbl>, n_unweighted <dbl>, deff <dbl>,
#> #   neff <dbl>, icc <dbl>, ci_method <chr>, method <chr>

write_vcs_report() writes the tables as CSVs or as one Excel workbook, ready for a Quarto, Word or Excel template of your choosing.
